sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who uses the gateway, what job does it do, and which numbers shape it?
criteria: Derives average and peak requests per second and tokens per minute from the monthly volume
Computes baseline monthly spend from the model mix at list prices
Names a headline metric that ties savings to equal eval quality
Treats full adoption by all 40 teams as a requirement

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the gateway as layers: what runs in each, what it hands to the next, and why it exists.
criteria: Separates edge, policy and admission, redaction, provider adapters and the usage log into layers
Includes a separate durable path for batch traffic
States one idea about what the gateway controls and what it must leave alone

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: What does the gateway need to know about teams, prices and providers, and how does it stay current?
criteria: Keeps a team registry with budget, priority, data class and allowed models
Versions prices by effective date instead of hardcoding them
Reads provider rate-limit and health signals per request
Reconciles computed cost against provider invoices

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: What does every request pass through, and how much time does each stage add?
criteria: Splits added latency by stage and the total fits 25 ms at p99
Reserves output tokens at admission and reconciles after completion
Streams responses through without buffering the whole answer
Keeps model calls out of the hot path

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: The gateway runs no agent, so what does it do for the agents that call it?
criteria: Enforces a per-run budget or call cap keyed by a run id
Detects repeated identical requests within a run
Propagates trace context to provider spans and usage events
Routes to cheaper models only on opt-in routes backed by the team's eval

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What state does the gateway keep, where, and for how long?
criteria: Keeps rate-limit and budget counters in a shared store with a durability plan
Uses session affinity to keep provider prompt caches warm
Declines to store conversation history, with a reason

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: Does the gateway expose or touch tools, and with what limits?
criteria: Passes teams' tool and MCP definitions through unchanged
Scopes any usage or budget tool to the caller's teams
Keeps budget increases behind a human approver in code

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What is the API surface, and how do you make sure every team uses it?
criteria: Offers provider-native pass-through or explains how provider features survive translation
Sizes the gateway fleet from the peak request rate
Provides a batch endpoint backed by a durable workflow
Blocks direct egress or rotates old keys to force adoption

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: Which cost levers save the most, and which are not worth it?
criteria: Shows monthly spend with each lever applied in order, with dollar savings
Quantifies prompt caching and routing separately
Uses provider batch pricing for offline traffic
Takes a position on semantic caching with its savings and its risk

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Which stores hold counters, policy and usage, and how big are they?
criteria: Sizes usage events per month and over the retention period
Uses an analytics store (for example ClickHouse) for attribution queries
Makes usage events idempotent so replays do not double-count
Keeps provider keys in a secrets manager and virtual keys hashed

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does the gateway return to callers, and what does it report to teams and finance?
criteria: Leaves the response body unchanged and adds metadata in headers
Returns cost or remaining limits per request
Produces a reconciled monthly chargeback by team and feature

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: What enforces budgets, limits and data rules if a team's code or prompt tries to bypass them?
criteria: Enforces 50/80/100% budget actions in gateway code
Handles 100% for customer-facing teams without causing an outage
Routes by data class and redacts PII before non-cleared providers
Sheds load by priority class under provider pressure

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: What number proves the gateway worked?
criteria: Gives baseline and target spend with the measurement source
Measures attribution coverage and adoption
Gates savings on eval scores staying flat

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, including the gateway itself, and what catches each failure?
criteria: Uses circuit breakers with stated thresholds and a fallback provider
Limits hedging to short calls and counts its cost
Decides fail-open or fail-closed per priority when the counter store fails
Covers the usage log being unavailable without losing events

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it, and what number unlocks each step?
criteria: Builds visibility and attribution before limits and savings
Ends each step with a measurable number
Migrates low-priority traffic first and keeps a rollback path
